title: bitopological-settling-site
description: The Grothendieck site (T*, J) on which the cohomology of a predication hyperdoctrine lives, assembled from fiberwise paired Priestley (pairwise-Stone) spaces over the contravariant predicate category and the covariant settling direction.

underlyingCategory.description: the category T*_site indexed by predicate object, settling stage, and pairwise-Stone clopen

objects.description: triples (q, tau, U) with q in C^op, tau < lambda an ordinal, and U a pairwise-Stone clopen in the paired Priestley space X_q^tau

morphisms.description: triples (f, h, j): f a C-morphism q -> q', h a lambda^op-morphism tau -> tau' (tau' >= tau), j an inclusion U' -> (f x h)^*(U) of pairwise-Stone clopens

composition.description: composition is taken componentwise across f, h, and j

topology.description: the Grothendieck topology J generated by a pairwise-Stone pretopology

coveringFamily.description: a family {(q, tau, U_i) -> (q, tau, U)} of pairwise-Stone inclusions at fixed (q, tau) covers iff union of U_i = U in the pairwise-Stone topology on X_q^tau

fiberCoversOnly.description: covers are only fiber-level refinements at fixed (q, tau); there are no temporal covers, cross-ordinal content is carried in morphisms and extracted as a direct limit

isBasis.description: pairwise-Stone covers are closed under pullback by Priestley morphisms, so the pretopology is a Grothendieck basis

regime.description: complexity regime by settling-bound cardinality kappa, controlling whether cohomology is finite-cellular, Cech-computable, transfinitely computable, or only a direct limit over bounded sub-sites
